newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Randstad sees little cost from pay deal.
newsitem.headline: Randstad sees little cost from pay deal.

text.p: Temporary employment agency Randstad NV said on Tuesday its new system of paying part-time workers, starting in mid-1997, would have a minimal cost.
Randstad said on Monday it had reached an agreement with the FNV Services Union in a dispute over its payment system.

A Randstad spokesman told Reuters that under the agreement, people working up to 25 hours per week would be paid gross, while those working more than 25 hours would continue to be paid net of tax and social security payments.
Concern that the gross-payment system would cut profit margins sparked a sharp fall in the share price last week.

But the spokesman said this concern arose from a mistaken belief the company was able to book as profit the money that part-time workers could otherwise reclaim from the tax and social security authorities.
He said it had not been understood that Randstad paid a supplement to workers under the net-payment system as an allowance for holidays, sick leave, short leave and other pay.
This represented most of the difference between gross and net pay, he said.
But the supplement would not be paid to workers paid gross under the new system.
"This will cost us money. But we have said it will be a very minimal cost," the spokesman said.
He declined to specify the cost except to say it would be "within the margins" allowed by analysts in their profit forecast models.
Randstand shares closed at 127.30 guilders, up 6.20 from the previous close.
